provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1962 reads `qui` where 1862 reads `qm`; 1962 reads `Moysi in` where 1862 reads `M6ysi m`; 1962 reads `Sinai,` where 1862 reads `Slnai,`; 1962 reads `eodem` where 1862 reads `e6dem`; 1962 reads `Catharinae Virginis` where 1862 reads `Catnarinae Vfreinis`; 1962 reads `mirabiliter` where 1862 reads `mirabfliter`; 1962 reads `quiesumus;` where 1862 reads `quaesumus;`; 1962 reads `meritis` where 1862 reads `m6ritis`; 1962 reads `intercessione,` where 1862 reads `intercessi6ne,`; 1962 reads `pervenire` where 1862 reads `pervenfre`; 1962 has `et regnat in unitate.`; 1862 has nothing there; 1862 sets commas after `loco` and after `tuos` that the 1962 does not, and none after the second `ut` or after `montem`; 1862 prints the j-orthography (ejus); 1862 conclusion is the short cue `Qui tecum vivit.`; the 1962 writes it out; 1862 layer damage: `qm` for qui, `m` for in, `Slnai`, `Catnarinae`, `Vfreinis`, `mirabfliter`, `pervenfre`; each is a serif or accent misread and each is clean in the 1962. Corroboration: 1922 Mame carries 25 November at PDF p. 877; not transcribed.

propers.text:
Suscipe, Domine, munera, quae in beatae N. Virginis et Martyris tuae
solemnitate deferimus: cujus nos confidimus patrocinio liberari. Per Dominum
nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.
